question: What comparison links recursive TraceGuard to nonrecursive evidence gating?

context_chunks.title: Recursive policy
context_chunks.text: The recursive TraceGuard policy obtains evidence through child calls and records child evidence handles for parent synthesis.

context_chunks.title: Nonrecursive policy
context_chunks.text: The nonrecursive evidence-gated policy cites retrieved chunks directly but does not perform recursive sub-call decomposition.

context_chunks.title: Comparison
context_chunks.text: Both policies can attach evidence, but only the recursive policy tests whether child-call provenance changes citation admissibility and repair behavior.

gold_answers: Both attach evidence, but recursive TraceGuard tests child-call provenance effects on admissibility and repair behavior.

question: Which condition isolates the value of TraceGuard when recursion is enabled?

context_chunks.title: Recursive no gate
context_chunks.text: The recursive-no-gate condition enables recursive decomposition but does not reject parent claims with missing evidence handles.

context_chunks.title: Recursive gate
context_chunks.text: The recursive-gate condition keeps recursion enabled and adds TraceGuard enforcement over cited child evidence handles.

gold_answers: Comparing recursive-no-gate with recursive-gate isolates the value of TraceGuard under recursion.
